captions.detailed: This 3D-printed flexible bracelet features a circular design with a hollow, segmented wall structure. The inner and outer walls are thin, concentric cylinders linked together by a series of repeating, triangular zig-zag internal ribs (spikes) that allow the structure to flex. Vertical slits are cut into both the inner and outer walls at alternating intervals to enable the bending motion, while custom extruded blocky text is embossed on the outer surface of several segments.
captions.instruction: Design a parametric flexible bracelet in OpenSCAD with customizable inner and outer radii, height, and number of segments. The bracelet should feature thin inner and outer cylindrical walls connected by internal zig-zag ribs, with vertical gap slits cut into the walls to allow flexibility, and support custom embossed or debossed text along the outer perimeter.
captions.factory: The script uses concentric cylinders (`cylinder` with `difference`) to define thin inner and outer circular bands. Vertical slits are cut into these bands using a loop of rotated `cube` primitives in the `innerholes` and `outerholes` modules. The connecting spring-like structures are created in the `spikes` module by generating 2D triangular connections with `polygon` using trigonometric coordinates and extruding them with `linear_extrude`. A custom font module extrudes and scales individual letters using `polygon` paths, placing them along the outer radius with calculated rotational offsets.
